title: Distinct Subsequences
summary: Count the ways to pick characters from s, in order, that spell out t.

tests.explain: Drop any one of the three b's from "rabbbit": 3 ways to spell "rabbit".
There are 5 ways to pick a b, then an a, then a g in order.
The empty string can be formed in exactly one way: pick nothing.

hints: A subsequence keeps the original order but may skip characters. Different sets of chosen positions count as different ways, even when they spell the same text.

Let dp[i][j] be the number of ways to form the first j characters of t from the first i characters of s. Look at the last character s[i-1]: you may always skip it, and if it equals t[j-1] you may also use it.

dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + (s[i-1] === t[j-1] ? dp[i-1][j-1] : 0). Base cases: dp[i][0] = 1 (the empty t can be formed one way) and dp[0][j] = 0 for j > 0. The answer is dp[m][n]; one row, filled right to left, is enough.
